land.text: the Congo: 'The Belgian Congo achieved independence on 30 June 1960 under the name Republic of the Congo.'

predecessors.note: The belgian-congo dossier records the same event as a split in June 1960 (Ruanda-Urundi stayed Belgian until 1 July 1962).

capitals.name: Léopoldville (Kinshasa)
capitals.note: 'Kinshasa, formerly Léopoldville. Mobutu renamed it in 1966.' The seat does not move.

capitals.name: Kinshasa
capitals.note: Same city under its new name; the rebel regimes of 1960-62 and 1964 sat at Stanleyville (Kisangani) and the State of Katanga at Élisabethville (Lubumbashi), not as capitals of this state.

rulers.name: Joseph Kasa-Vubu
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: The page gives no start date; he was president when he dismissed Lumumba on 5 September 1960, and the Congo Crisis page ends the crisis with Mobutu's coup of 25 November 1965.

rulers.name: Mobutu Sese Seko
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Seized power in 1965 and ruled until he fled into exile in 1997'; the country was renamed Zaire in 1971.

rulers.name: Joseph Kabila
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: Succeeded his father in 2001 and 'stepped down in 2019' (swearing-in of his successor on 24 January 2019).

rulers.name: Félix Tshisekedi
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'officially sworn in as president on 24 January' 2019; re-elected December 2023.

keyframe_review.note: 2,307,868 km2 against the infobox 2,345,409 km2 (no year; ratio 0.98). The whole country as independent on 30 June 1960. This is the de jure shape: Katanga (from 11 July) and South Kasai (from 8 August) seceded within weeks, and the ledger's loss events take them out (rule 5) rather than a second keyframe.

2,307,723 km2 for 1961-1962: the de jure country. De facto the State of Katanga stood until January 1963 and South Kasai until 5 October 1962 (ledger loss and gain), and the Stanleyville government (Free Republic of the Congo) held Orientale and parts of Kivu, Maniema and Sankuru from December 1960 to January 1962 (ledger losses and one gain against free-republic-of-the-congo). fx-29 (F134): the keyframe drew the de jure country, so in 1961 the compiler's keyframe snap took Orientale and Bukavu back from the Free Republic (1,839 cells) and Katanga from the State of Katanga (1,310) and the size rule gave them back; the shape now matches the ledger's losses of 1960-61 (Free Republic page: 'On 12 December 1960, Gizenga declared his new government', 'On 24 December, Stanleyville troops occupied Bukavu', 'Pro-Gizenga administrators were installed in the Maniema and Sankuru districts, while Orientale and Kivu-based army units seemed to be under his control'; Congo Crisis page: Katanga 11 July 1960 to 17 January 1963, South Kasai 8 August 1960 to 5 October 1962).

minus.text: the lands the central government did not hold at the start of 1961: the Stanleyville government's Orientale, Bukavu, northern Kivu, Sankuru and Maniema, the State of Katanga and South Kasai

correction.text: the de facto country in 1961: Cliopatria's shape without the Free Republic of the Congo's lands (Gizenga declared it on 12 December 1960; it was 'not fully reintegrated ... until Gizenga was arrested in January 1962'), without Katanga (seceded 11 July 1960, ended 17 January 1963) and without South Kasai (8 August 1960 to 5 October 1962). The ledger's gains of January, October 1962 and January 1963 bring them back.

keyframe_review.note: 2,307,781 km2 for 1963-1966: the unified country after Katanga's end on 17 January 1963. The Simba rebellion of 1964 (ledger contest, July to November) is the only dated change of control; Mobutu's coup of 25 November 1965 changes the ruler, not the land.
2,307,837 km2 for 1967-1972, the same land as the later shapes. The page records the 1971 rename to Zaire ('In 1971, Mobutu renamed the country the Republic of Zaire') as a name change only.

correction.text: The same state under the name Zaire (1971-1997): 'In 1971, Mobutu renamed the country the Republic of Zaire'; Cliopatria draws these years as a separate row 'Zaire' (2,307,837 km2) with the same land as the Democratic Republic of the Congo shapes on either side

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe under this slug: Cliopatria has no Democratic Republic of the Congo shape for 1973-1995 because the years sit in its 'Zaire' row (Wikidata Q6500954, same Seshat id cg_congo_democratic_rep). It is one state with a rename (ledger 1971 and 1997), so these years belong to this dossier; if a separate 'zaire' dossier is also written, the integrator should keep one of the two. 'Zaire' is deliberately not listed in cliopatria_names so that the two agents' files do not both claim its shapes.

2,307,837 km2 for 1996-2023: the whole country. The First Congo War ('24 October 1996 to 16 May 1997') brought the AFDL to power and 'Zaire renamed back to the Democratic Republic of the Congo'; the Second Congo War (1998-2003) divided control between the government, rebels and foreign armies without a dated zone map on the page, so these are ledger contests, not new shapes.

2,307,837 km2, the same land. The page says Goma 'was occupied by the M23 rebels in 2012 and again since 2025' and that M23 captured Bukavu in early 2025: both after or outside the 2024 shape, not drawn.

ledger.note: 1960: the Congo becomes independent from Belgium. 'The Belgian Congo achieved independence on 30 June 1960 under the name Republic of the Congo' (briefly 'Republic of the Congo-Léopoldville' to tell it from its neighbour).

region.text: Katanga, whose State of Katanga Tshombe declared on 11 July 1960

ledger.note: 1960: Katanga secedes under Moise Tshombe. 'On 11 July 1960,' he declared Katanga independent as the State of Katanga (State of Katanga infobox area 496,871 km2, capital Elisabethville). The northern Katanga clashes that began 'from late 1960 onwards' are not placed by the pages.

region.text: 'a section of Kasai Province situated slightly to the north of Katanga', around Bakwanga (Mbuji-Mayi)

ledger.note: 1960: South Kasai declares its autonomy. 'on 8 August, a section of Kasai Province situated slightly to the north of Katanga also declared its autonomy.' The page names no boundary; the South Kasai page dates the proclamation 9 August 1960; the 100 km radius round Bakwanga (Mbuji-Mayi) is the researcher's reading.

region.text: Orientale Province, the base of the Stanleyville government

ledger.note: 1960: Antoine Gizenga's Free Republic of the Congo takes Orientale. 'On 12 December 1960, Gizenga declared his new government, the Free Republic of the Congo,' 'based in Orientale Province'; the Congo Crisis page says the rebel government formed 'in November 1960'.
24 December 1960: 'Stanleyville troops occupied Bukavu and arrested the local army commander.' The 50 km radius is a reading.

January 1961: 'Gizenga's authority was also established over the Sankuru District of Kasai Province.' The page places the sentence between 'By 10 January, Stanleyville forces had occupied northern Katanga as far in as Manono' and 'Around then, control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region', so the month is January 1961 (reviewer af-08-f, 2026-10-19; previously undated at confidence 1). The Lodja radius is a reading of the district.

region.text: Goma and the northern Kivu region

ledger.note: By 10 January 1961 'control had been consolidated in Goma and the northern Kivu region.'
October 1961: 'Pro-Gizenga administrators were installed in the Maniema and Sankuru districts.'

region.text: Orientale, Bukavu, northern Kivu, Sankuru and Maniema: 'not fully reintegrated into the Republic of the Congo until Gizenga was arrested in January 1962'

ledger.note: January 1962: the Stanleyville government ends. The Congo Crisis page: 'the Gizenga government however collapsed in January 1962 after Gizenga was arrested'; the Free Republic page: censured on 15 January, flown to Léopoldville on 20 January, infobox 'Disestablished: 16 January 1962'. Gizenga had joined Adoula's coalition government on 2 August 1961 but returned to Stanleyville in September.
1962: the central army enters Bakwanga and South Kasai's secession ends. 'On 5 October 1962, central government troops again arrived in Bakwanga' after a coup there on 29-30 September 1962.

1963: Katanga's secession ends. 'on 17 January 1963, Tshombe surrendered his final stronghold of Kolwezi, effectively ending the Katangese secession.' The State of Katanga page has Tshombe conceding on 15 January and gives dissolution as 21 January 1963.

region.text: the towns the Simbas took: 'Port-Émpain, Stanleyville, Paulis and Lisala between July and August', with Albertville later recaptured (Port-Empain is Kindu, Paulis is Isiro, Albertville is Kalemie)

ledger.counterpart: People's Republic of the Congo (Simba rebels)
ledger.note: 1964: the Simba rebellion takes the east and north. 'The rebels founded a state, the People's Republic of the Congo,' with its capital at Stanleyville; they 'took control of a significant amount of territory'. The page lists towns by their colonial names, not an extent; the modern names (Kindu, Isiro, Kalemie) and the radii are the researcher's reading. The earlier Kwilu Rebellion 'broke out on 16 January 1964 in the cities of Idiofa and Gungu' with no territory named.

ledger.counterpart: People's Republic of the Congo (Simba rebels)
ledger.note: 1964: Stanleyville falls to the army. Belgian paratroopers landed in Stanleyville on 24 November (Operation Dragon Rouge); 'Soon after Dragon Rouge, ANC and mercenary troops captured Stanleyville, putting an end to the Simba rebellion.' Albertville and Lisala had been recaptured in late August and early September.

1971: Mobutu renames the country the Republic of Zaire. 'In 1971, Mobutu renamed the country the Republic of Zaire.' Cliopatria draws 1973-1995 under its separate 'Zaire' row; it is the same state and land (rule 2).

region.text: eastern Zaire along the border with Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi: 'Kabila's AFDL was able to capture 800 x 100 km of territory along the border with Rwanda, Uganda, and Burundi by 25 December 1996'

ledger.counterpart: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)
ledger.note: 1996: the First Congo War begins in the east. The page gives the war as '24 October 1996 to 16 May 1997' and 'The war began when Rwanda invaded eastern Zaire in 1996'; the Banyamulenge rebellion began 31 August 1996. The page does not name Goma, Bukavu or Uvira, so the Kivu provinces are the researcher's reading of the border strip.

region.text: eastern Zaire; the AFDL had by then taken Lubumbashi (19 April) and entered Kinshasa

ledger.counterpart: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)
ledger.note: 1997: the AFDL takes the whole country. 'Mobutu fled Kinshasa on May 16, and the rebels entered the capital without serious resistance'; Kabila 'proclaimed himself president on 17 May'. The sweep across the country (Kisangani, Boende and Mbandaka undated; Lubumbashi 19 April) is not given a date per town by the page, so the war is drawn as one eastern contest that ends with the regime.

1997: Zaire is renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo under Laurent-Désiré Kabila. Infobox result 'Zaire renamed back to the Democratic Republic of the Congo; Installation of Laurent-Désiré Kabila as President'; the page says Kabila reorganised the nation as the DRC right after proclaiming himself president on 17 May. Month is the page's sequence, not a stated date.

region.text: 'the resource-rich eastern provinces' under the RCD, 'Uganda-controlled Kisangani' from April 1999, and 'the north of the country' under the MLC from November 1998

ledger.counterpart: RCD and MLC rebels with Rwanda and Uganda
ledger.note: 1998: the Second Congo War divides the country. The war 'began on 2 August 1998'; the RCD 'quickly came to dominate the resource-rich eastern provinces, and based its operations in Goma'; in November 1998 a Ugandan-backed MLC 'was reported in the north'; Zimbabwean, Angolan and Namibian forces fought for the government. The page gives no dated zone map; the three eastern provinces are the researcher's reading, and the MLC's north (not named) is not drawn.

region.text: the eastern provinces and Kisangani area under rebel and foreign control

ledger.counterpart: RCD and MLC rebels with Rwanda and Uganda
ledger.note: 2003: a unified transitional government ends the war. 'On 18 July 2003, the Transitional Government came into being'; Rwanda announced the completion of its withdrawal on 5 October 2002 (Pretoria Accord of 30 July 2002), Uganda signed the Luanda Agreement on 6 September 2002 and the Zimbabweans had left by the end of 2002. The Ituri and Kivu conflicts continue (infobox territorial changes).

wars.name: Congo Crisis
wars.outcome: Infobox: 'The Congo established as an independent unitary state under the authoritarian presidency of Mobutu Sese Seko.' Katanga reintegrated January 1963, South Kasai 5 October 1962, the Stanleyville governments crushed in January 1962 and November 1964.
wars.note: Infobox dates '5 July 1960 – 25 November 1965'. Belgium deployed paratroopers 'without the Congolese state's permission' from 9 July 1960.

wars.name: Simba rebellion
belligerents: People's Republic of the Congo (Simba rebels)
wars.outcome: The army and mercenaries retook Stanleyville soon after Operation Dragon Rouge of 24 November 1964, 'putting an end to the Simba rebellion'.
wars.note: Part of the Congo Crisis page; listed separately because the ledger carries its own contest. The page does not date the end of fighting beyond Stanleyville.

wars.name: First Congo War
belligerents: Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL)

zones.text: the border strip with Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi taken by 25 December 1996

wars.outcome: 'Mobutu fled Kinshasa on May 16'; Laurent-Désiré Kabila proclaimed himself president on 17 May 1997 and Zaire was renamed the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
wars.note: Infobox period 24 October 1996 - 16 May 1997 as the page words it; Ugandan forces joined the invasion (DRC page).

wars.name: Second Congo War
belligerents: Movement for the Liberation of Congo (MLC)

zones.text: the eastern provinces under the RCD and Kisangani under Uganda

wars.outcome: Infobox 'Military stalemate'; Lusaka Ceasefire signed July 1999, Pretoria Accord 30 July 2002, Luanda Agreement 6 September 2002, Transitional Government 18 July 2003 with Joseph Kabila as president.
wars.note: Infobox territorial changes: 'Continuation of the Ituri conflict' and 'Start of the Kivu conflict'. The page has no dated zone map.

certainty.note: The international frontier is the colonial line inherited from the Belgian Congo (no border page was opened, so this rests on the dossier belgian-congo and the absence of any dispute on the DRC page). The approximate zones are the rebel and foreign-held lands of 1960-63, 1964 and 1996-2003, whose extents the pages give only as towns and provinces.

notes: ZAIRE ROW: Cliopatria has the same state in two rows, 'Democratic Republic of the Congo' 1960-1972 and 1996-2024 and 'Zaire' 1973-1995 (Wikidata Q6500954, Seshat id cg_congo_democratic_rep shared with this row); the brief's collision list pairs Q974 with the Republic of the Congo, but those are different states (see below). This dossier covers all 1960-2024 and carries the 1973-1995 years in a new keyframe that points at the Zaire shape; the Zaire row is not listed in cliopatria_names. If an af-08 'zaire' dossier exists, the integrator should keep one. Q974 COLLISION: the Republic of the Congo (Brazzaville, Cliopatria row republic-of-the-congo, 1961-2024) is a different state from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (Kinshasa); Cliopatria gives both rows the id Q974, but the DRC page says the country was briefly called 'Republic of the Congo-Léopoldville' to tell it 'from its neighbour', i.e. a different state, so the shared id is a Cliopatria error. Two dossiers, no merge. Cliopatria: six shapes, 2,307,723-2,307,868 km2, the same bbox; the differences are grid noise. Shapes are the de jure country: Katanga (11 July 1960 - 17 January 1963) and South Kasai (8 August 1960 - 5 October 1962) are removed by loss and gain events against the counterparts state-of-katanga and south-kasai, so the rebel dossiers must exist for the colour to show; the Stanleyville regime (December 1960 - January 1962) is carried by losses and a gain against free-republic-of-the-congo (a rebel dossier written in this batch); the Simba rebels (July - November 1964) are a contest only because their land is not on the pages. Not covered (page budget of five pages, all spent): the Shaba invasions of the 1970s (no page opened dates them), the Kwilu rebellion's zone, the Ituri conflict, the M23 occupation of Goma in 2012 (the DRC page gives only the year), the 2025 M23 conquests (after the dossier's last year), and the 1960 Belgian paratroop landings beyond what the Congo Crisis page says. Rebel dossiers written in this batch: state-of-katanga, south-kasai, free-republic-of-the-congo. Counterparts still needing dossiers: the People's Republic of the Congo of the Simba rebels (1964, months only), the AFDL, RCD and MLC (rebel movements, held land 1996-2003). Infobox area 2,345,409 km2 (no year) against Cliopatria 2,307,868 km2, ratio 0.98. Native names: the page gives languages (Kikongo ya leta, Lingala, Swahili, Luba-Kasai) but no native name of the state.
